# Sparse Voxel DAGs

Also called: SVDAG, Sparse Voxel Directed Acyclic Graph

## Overview
Sparse Voxel DAGs (SVDAGs) are a memory-efficient 3D data structure that extends the Sparse Voxel Octree (SVO) by merging identical subtrees into shared nodes, forming a Directed Acyclic Graph [G]. While SVOs efficiently encode spatial sparsity, they store redundant copies of identical non-empty geometry, leading to high memory consumption at high resolutions [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md]. SVDAGs solve this by allowing multiple parent nodes to share pointers to the same child instance, achieving [lossless compression](#5360-entropy-encoding.md) of topological redundancy without decompression overhead during traversal [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md]. This sets them apart from siblings like [Compact pointer tree](844-compact-pointer-tree.md) or [OpenVDB (VDB)](1508-openvdb-vdb.md), which focus on spatial sparsity or [pointer compression](#1770-pointer-compression.md) rather than structural isomorphism [G].

## Shared principles
The family shares a bottom-up reduction mechanism that converts a tree into a DAG to eliminate duplicate subtrees [G].
1. **Node Identity:** Two nodes are considered identical if they have the same `childmask` (encoding the existence of 8 children) and identical pointers to their respective children [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
2. **Bottom-Up Reduction:** The reduction process iterates from the leaves up to the root. At each level, nodes are sorted by their identity key (childmask + child pointers) to group identical nodes together [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
3. **Compaction and Indirection:** Identical nodes are compacted into a single unique instance. An indirection table maps original node positions to their unique counterparts, and parent pointers are updated to reference these unique instances [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].

## Subtopics

### [Bottom-up SVO to DAG Reduction](898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md)
A method for compressing an SVO into a minimal DAG by merging identical subtrees. It handles memory constraints by processing sub-DAGs for large resolutions and guarantees the smallest possible DAG within $L$ iterations. Choose this when geometry has high topological redundancy.

### [Pointerless Sparse Voxel Directed Acyclic Graph (PSVDAG)](949-pointerless-sparse-voxel-directed-acyclic-graph-psvdag.md)
A variant defined by BNF where nodes are either Inner or Leaf nodes, removing explicit pointer storage. Choose this for cache-friendly, pointer-free traversal at the cost of indirection logic.

### [Sparse Voxel DAG Ray Traversal](1147-sparse-voxel-dag-ray-traversal.md)
A GPU-based traversal method for visibility queries and primary [ray intersection](#7624-ray-ray-intersection.md). It simplifies the SVO loop by removing contour tests and extends [beam optimization](#932-beam-optimization.md) to soft shadows via reverse beam tracing. Choose this for real-time rendering on GPUs.

### [Isomorphic Node Recycling (DAOG)](3422-isomorphic-node-recycling-daog.md)
A [compression](#4-compression.md) method that reuses structurally identical nodes by converting the Octree into a Directed Acyclic Octal Graph. Choose this as an alternative implementation of the DAG reduction principle.

## Background
The [Sparse Voxel DAG](#5984-sparse-voxel-dag.md) was introduced by Laine and Karras in 2010 as an extension of the Sparse Voxel Octree [G]. It addresses the memory bottleneck of SVOs at high resolutions (e.g., $128K^3$ grids) by exploiting the fact that complex 3D scenes often contain repeated geometric patterns [898-bottom-up-svo-to-dag-reduction.md].
